mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which positively impacts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns during periods of declining unemployment, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5%, it indicates monetary tightening, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) increases by more than 0.5% in one month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases, it signals a tightening labor market and higher borrowing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by > 0.5% in 1 month AND UNRATE decreases
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns despite the specified trigger conditions, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in retail sales (RSAFS) during a late-cycle expansion signals overextension in consumer spending, which may lead to a correction in equity markets, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns following a sharp increase in RSAFS, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals strong economic activity, which positively impacts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns during periods of rising industrial production, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals a strong labor market, which positively impacts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns following a significant increase in PAYEMS, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth exceeds industrial production (INDPRO) growth, it signals demand outpacing supply, leading to inflationary pressures and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns when GDP growth exceeds industrial production growth, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a monetary easing cycle, which reduces borrowing costs and stimulates economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns following a decrease in FEDFUNDS, this hypothesis is falsified.
